title: The natural fixed-sector paired-Gram and joint determinant-square polynomials are not stable in general
input: A is the 4x4 directed-cycle permutation matrix with entries in {0,1}; k=2. Define H(x)=sum_{|S|=2} det(G[P(S),P(S)]) x^S and P(x,y)=sum_{|I|=|J|=2,I disjoint J} det(A[I,J])^2 x^I y^J.
claim: H=x1*x3+x2*x4 and P=x1*x3*y2*y4+x2*x4*y1*y3. Borcea-Branden-Liggett Theorem 4.1 implies every real multiaffine stable polynomial has nonnegative Rayleigh differences; Delta_13 H and Delta_(x1,y2) P equal -1 at all variables 1. Both polynomials are therefore unstable. A is orthogonal, so kappa_2(A)=1.
proof: For a permutation matrix, det(A[I,J]) is nonzero iff J=pi(I), in which case its square is 1. At half filling in the directed 4-cycle, disjointness leaves exactly the two alternating classes. Direct differentiation gives the two negative Rayleigh differences.
costs: The witness has constant dimension, 0/1 entries, exact integer coefficients, and no numerical conditioning issue.
falsifier: A direct enumeration finds a third nonzero disjoint minor pair, or either Rayleigh difference is nonnegative at the all-ones point.
scope_limit: Refutes stability of these natural polynomials as a blanket premise only. It does not rule out another representation, an algorithm using the supplied matrix, or non-stable coefficient extraction.
evidence: evidence/verify_cycle_counterexample.py and evidence/cycle_fixture.json; finite cycle replay n=4,6,8

title: Paired-Gram polynomial stability and exact evaluation for independent 2-site off-diagonal blocks
input: n=2s and a supplied site partition makes A=direct-sum_b [[0,a_b],[b_b,0]], with a_b,b_b nonnegative rationals. The target is Z_k for 0<=k<=s.
claim: Writing L_b=a_b^2*x_(b,L)+b_b^2*x_(b,R) and c_b=a_b^2+b_b^2, the paired-Gram polynomial H_k(x)=e_k(L_1,...,L_s) is real stable when nonzero, and Z_k=e_k(c_1,...,c_s).
proof: A nonzero block minor uses one row and one opposite column; selecting both sites violates disjointness. Block factorization gives the elementary-symmetric identities. For Im(x)>0, each nonzero L_b(x) has positive imaginary part, and e_k is stable by its product-of-linear-factors representation and Gauss-Lucas.
costs: A descending coefficient DP uses O(sk) rational operations. If L is total input bit length and D is the product of entry denominators, log D<=L; output numerator and denominator have O(kL+s) and O(kL) bits. A conservative schoolbook bit-time bound is O(sk(kL+s)^2). Exact suffix DP samples the target in expected polynomial fair-bit time. The joint row/column polynomial P_k can still fail stability, already for one block with a_1=b_1=1.
normalization: The fixed-sector unfiltered norm is S_k=[t^k] product_b(1+t*a_b^2)(1+t*b_b^2), and physical Gutzwiller acceptance after number-sector preparation is Z_k/S_k. The full unnormalized BCS denominator is product_b(1+a_b^2)(1+b_b^2). These can be exponentially small as probabilities; physical retries cost expected 1/p. The classical exact sampler has no physical postselection cost.
falsifier: A block-compatible disjoint minor that uses two selected sites in a 2-site block, or an exact coefficient that disagrees with the stated elementary-symmetric polynomial.
scope_limit: This is a structural subclass with a supplied block partition, not a general sparse-matrix result; stability alone is not used as a counting oracle.
evidence: Proof and exact recurrence in RESULT.txt

title: Uniform importance sampling is an FPRAS under support-density and weight-ratio promises
input: Explicit nonnegative rational A, 0<=k<=n/2, Omega={(I,J): |I|=|J|=k, I disjoint J}, N=|Omega|. Supplied promises rho=|{w>0}|/N>=rho_0 and max(w>0)/min(w>0)<=R_0, with R_0/rho_0 polynomial in n and input bit length.
claim: Uniform exact sampling from Omega and exact evaluation of w=det(A[I,J])^2, followed by a median-of-means estimator of N*E[w], returns a relative-epsilon estimate of Z_k with probability at least 1-delta using O((R_0/rho_0)*epsilon^-2*log(1/delta)) samples.
proof: E[w^2]/E[w]^2<=w_max*N/Z<=R_0/rho_0. Chebyshev gives constant success per O((R_0/rho_0)/epsilon^2)-sample group; a median of O(log(1/delta)) groups amplifies confidence.
costs: Clear rational denominators once. Bareiss computes each minor in O(k^3) integer operations with O(k(L+log k))-bit intermediates, yielding conservative O(k^5(L+log k)^2) bit operations per sample; output rational height is polynomial. Total sample and bit costs are detailed in RESULT.txt. The promise is not verified by the algorithm.
normalization: For arbitrary rational A, S_k=[t^k]det(I+t*A^T*A) gives fixed-sector acceptance Z_k/S_k; det(I+A^T*A) is the full BCS norm. S_k is exactly computable in polynomial bit time. Physical postselection retries still cost 1/p, separately from estimator runtime.
falsifier: The second-moment inequality or the exact uniform proposal distribution fails, or the supplied rho_0,R_0 do not bound support density and positive weight ratio.
scope_limit: This is a promised-class FPRAS only. No polynomial-time verifier for the promises and no generic importance sampler are claimed.

title: Every fixed atom-probe list for all half-filled directed-cycle instances is exponential
input: Even n=2q, k=q; inputs range over directed Hamilton-cycle permutation matrices, and a probe tests one individual legal minor pair (I,J).
claim: Any input-independent atom list that hits every nonzero target on this family has at least binom(n,n/2)/2 atoms. Any fixed proposal has an instance with support mass at most 2/binom(n,n/2); m atom probes cannot guarantee 2/3 hit probability unless m>=binom(n,n/2)/3.
proof: Each input support is {(S,S^c),(S^c,S)} for the alternating classes of its cycle. Every balanced S can be made an alternating class by ordering S and S^c alternately around a Hamilton cycle. Complement pairs partition the legal atom universe into binom(n,n/2)/2 disjoint possible supports. On the all-zero transcript before the first hit, an atom-probe algorithm that sees only prior queried weights follows one common query path; m queries cover at most m complementary classes.
costs: The lower bound is exponential in n because binom(n,n/2)>=2^n/(n+1). The instances have 0/1 entries, Z=2, and matrix condition number 1.
falsifier: A cycle input has additional positive atom pairs beyond its alternating classes, or a legal atom belongs to two different complement classes.
scope_limit: This applies to input-independent term-probe lists or black-box probes whose choices depend only on previous queried weights. It does not apply to algebraic evaluations aggregating terms or algorithms that inspect and exploit A; the cycle itself has a linear-time exact solution.
evidence: Combinatorial proof in RESULT.txt; cycle replay n=4,6,8 and two-block evaluator replay in evidence/cycle_fixture.json
